title: Inject social-preview meta tags into HTML <head>
description:
**Problem.** Pages built by the HTML plugin have no Open Graph, Twitter Card, or canonical metadata, so every rheo site previews as a bare URL in Twitter/X, Discord, Slack, iMessage, Mastodon and LinkedIn. Nothing in `rheo.toml` or in a `.typ` source can currently put a `<meta>` tag in the head.

**Why it can't be done downstream.** Typst's exporter (`typst-html-0.15.0/src/document.rs:313-362`, `head_element`) emits exactly and only: `<meta charset>`, `<meta viewport>`, `<title>` (from `info.title`), `<meta name="description">` (from `info.description`), `<meta name="authors">`, `<meta name="keywords">`. Elements authored via `html.elem("meta", ...)` in a `.typ` are NOT hoisted — no hoisting logic exists in typst-html (`finalize_dom`, `document.rs:252-311`, special-cases only `tag::html` and `tag::body`) nor in rheo (`grep -rn hoist crates/` is empty), and html5ever's re-parse inserts an in-body `<meta>` at the current node rather than relocating it. Typst's custom-DOM mode (`typst-html-0.15.0/src/lib.rs:56-57`) would let an author hand-write `<head>`, but both custom-DOM branches call `footnotes_unsupported_with_custom_dom` (`document.rs:364-380`), so footnotes become a hard compile error — unacceptable for prose sites.

## PHASE 1 — interactive design session with Lachlan

Do this first; do not skip to code. Six open questions. Work through them with him, then record the decisions as a comment on this bead before implementing.

1. **Config surface.** Three candidate shapes:
   - (a) *typed* — a `[html.social]` table with named keys (`site_name`, `og_image`, `og_image_alt`, `twitter_card`, `theme_color`, ...). Discoverable, validated, but every new tag needs a rheo release.
   - (b) *generic* — an `[html.head]` array of raw tag specs, e.g. `[[html.head]] tag = "meta"; property = "og:type"; content = "article"`. Maximally flexible, zero validation, users hand-write OG boilerplate.
   - (c) *hybrid* — typed keys for the social common case plus a generic passthrough for everything else (favicon, `rel=me`, verification tokens).

   Pick one. (c) is the likely answer, but the split point needs deciding.

2. **Base URL.** Absolute URLs are mandatory for `og:image` and strongly preferred for `og:url`/canonical — relative values are ignored by most scrapers. Today the only base is `feed_base_url` (`crates/html/src/lib.rs:191`, normalized in `HtmlConfig::base_url()` at `lib.rs:197-201`). Decide: generalize to a plain `base_url` with `feed_base_url` kept as a deprecated alias, or keep reading `feed_base_url` and accept the naming wart. Also decide the behaviour when no base URL is configured — skip social tags entirely, or emit the relative-safe subset.

3. **Per-page overrides and precedence.** Available inputs per page, all already on `CastVertebra` (`crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:91-107`): `title: String`, `date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, `vars: HashMap<String, RheoValue>` (harvested `rheo-*` variables), `output_path`, `bytes`. Note there is NO `metadata` field — but `#set document(description: ...)` already lands in the built head as `<meta name="description">`, so the injector can simply read it back out of the DOM instead of plumbing a new field through the parser. Proposed precedence, to confirm: `rheo-og-*` var, then the value read from the generated head (`<title>`, `<meta name="description">`), then the site-wide config default. Decide the var names (`rheo-og-image`, `rheo-og-description`, `rheo-og-type`, ...).

4. **Default-on vs opt-in.** Should rheo emit `og:title`/`og:url`/`og:type` + `twitter:card` automatically whenever a base URL is set, with zero config? That gives every existing rheo site working previews on upgrade, and argues for default-on with config only for the parts rheo cannot infer (`og:image`, `site_name`).

5. **Exact tag set.** Baseline proposal: `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:type` (`website` for the feed-excluded index, `article` elsewhere — or a var), `og:site_name`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:image` plus `og:image:width`/`:height`/`:alt`, `twitter:card` (`summary_large_image` when an image exists, else `summary`), `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`, and `theme-color` (Discord tints its embed sidebar from it). Decide whether favicon / `apple-touch-icon` / `manifest` links belong in this feature or a follow-up bead. Watch the attribute kind: Open Graph uses `property="og:..."` while Twitter uses `name="twitter:..."`, so the API needs both.

6. **Image generation out of scope?** Confirm the site supplies its own `og:image` file (via `[html.assets] copy`) and that rheo does not grow a card renderer in this bead.

## PHASE 2 — implementation

Where each change goes:

- `crates/core/src/util/html.rs` — the insertion machinery already exists and should be reused, not reinvented. `Element::create_element(tag, attrs)` (`html.rs:219-236`) is already generic over attributes; add public `Element::create_meta_property(property, content)` and `Element::create_meta_name(name, content)` beside `create_feed_link` (`html.rs:240`), `create_link` (`html.rs:253`) and `create_script` (`html.rs:258`). Add `HtmlDom::inject_head_meta(&[...])` modelled directly on `inject_head_links` (`html.rs:131-167`): find `<head>`, compute `head.last_meta_index().map(|i| i + 1).unwrap_or(0)` (`last_meta_index`, `html.rs:276-286`), then `insert_child_at` with an incrementing offset so declaration order is preserved. Also add two readers, `HtmlDom::title_text()` and `HtmlDom::meta_content(name)`, so values can be sourced from the head Typst already generated (see design Q3).

- `crates/html/src/lib.rs` — extend `HtmlConfig` (`lib.rs:188-194`) with the keys chosen in Q1. In `compile()`, build the per-output tag list and call `inject_head_meta` inside the existing `let mut dom = output.html()?` block (`lib.rs:142-160`), before `dom.serialize()`. CRITICAL: the `needs_head_links` gate at `lib.rs:140` and the `if needs_head_links || feed_link.is_some()` condition at `lib.rs:143` guard a fast path (`lib.rs:161-165`) that skips DOM work entirely; social tags must be added to that condition or they silently vanish on projects with no CSS/JS and no feed.

- `crates/core/src/build.rs:321-343` — the dev-server/watch path duplicates the head-injection logic. Either mirror the change there or, better, factor both call sites onto one shared helper so `rheo watch` and `rheo compile` cannot drift.

- `crates/html/src/feed.rs:148` — builds an entry URL as `format!("{}/{}", base_url.trim_end_matches('/'), output.output_path)`. The canonical/`og:url` construction is identical; factor it into one shared `entry_url(base, path)` rather than writing it twice.

**Tests.** Unit tests in `crates/core/src/util/html.rs` (a `#[cfg(test)]` block is already present): assert the injected `<meta>` lands after the last existing `<meta>` and before the injected `<link>`s; assert `property=` vs `name=` is chosen correctly per tag; assert declaration order survives. Add a fixture-level test compiling a small project with social config and asserting the emitted head byte-for-byte, including the no-base-URL and no-image fallbacks.

**Docs.** Update the `[html]` key table in `rheo-author/SKILL.md` and the config page on rheo.ohrg.org. While there: `rheo-author/SKILL.md:120-126` and `rheo.ohrg.org/pages/packages.typ:38` both document `css_stylesheets` (plural), but the registered asset name is `css_stylesheet` (singular) — `crates/html/src/lib.rs:51-52` — and `grep -rn css_stylesheets crates/` is empty. Fix that typo in the same pass.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Design decisions for Q1-Q6 are recorded on this bead before implementation starts.
2. `rheo compile . --html` on a project with the new config emits the agreed `og:*` / `twitter:*` / canonical tags into every page's `<head>`, with absolute URLs.
3. Per-page title and description are correct per page, not site-wide constants.
4. Projects with no social config still build byte-identically to before, or gain only the zero-config defaults agreed in Q4.
5. `rheo watch` produces the same head as `rheo compile`.
6. Validated against real scrapers: Twitter/X Card Validator, Discord (paste the URL), Facebook Sharing Debugger, plus `curl -A 'Twitterbot' <url>` to confirm the tags are in the static HTML and do not depend on JS.
7. Unit and fixture tests pass; SKILL.md and rheo.ohrg.org updated.

## Downstream consumer

`/home/lox/code/writing/sites/ohrg.org` is the first site to adopt this. Its Netlify build (`build.sh`) downloads the rheo release binary whose tag matches `version` in `rheo.toml`, so shipping this requires a tagged release and a version bump in that file. That site has no image in `static/` yet, so it will also need a 1200x630 card authored — its palette is in `style.css:16-29` (`--primary-color: #9ABDDC`, `--bg-color: #fdfdfd`, `--text-color: #1a1a1a`, Inter).

title: Emit Atom <published> from the vertebra date
description:
**Problem.** `crates/html/src/feed.rs` never emits an `atom:published` element. A vertebra's `#set document(date:)` — parsed into `CastVertebra.date` (`crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs:103-104`) — is the date the piece was written and published, but `generate_feed` maps it onto the entry's `updated` field instead (`feed.rs:117-133`), and `AtomEntry::to_atom` (`feed.rs:59-73`) calls only `entry.set_updated(...)`. `AtomEntry` (`feed.rs:14-22`) has no `published` field at all.

RFC 4287 distinguishes the two. Section 4.2.9: `atom:published` is "an instant associated with an event early in the life cycle of the entry — typically, associated with the initial creation or first availability of the resource". Section 4.2.15: `atom:updated` is the "most recent instant in time when an entry was modified in a way the publisher considers significant". `updated` is REQUIRED on every entry; `published` is optional. Feed readers (NetNewsWire, Reeder, Feedbin, Miniflux) prefer `published` for display and sort order when it is present. Emitting a creation date as `updated` with no `published` is therefore both semantically wrong and lossy.

## Fix

1. `crates/html/src/feed.rs:14-22` — add `pub published: Option<DateTime<Utc>>` to `AtomEntry`.

2. `crates/html/src/feed.rs:59-73` — in `to_atom`, call `entry.set_published(...)` with the fixed-offset value when `Some`, leaving it unset when `None`. Verify the `atom_syndication` signature first; the crate's `Entry::set_published` takes an `impl Into<Option<FixedDateTime>>`, so passing the `Option` directly is likely correct and no `if let` is needed.

3. `crates/html/src/feed.rs:103-159` — in the per-output loop, populate `published` with this precedence: a `rheo-feed-published` var (an RFC 3339 string, parsed and error-reported exactly like the existing `rheo-feed-updated` handling at `feed.rs:117-121`), then `output.date`, then `None`.

## Do NOT change how `updated` is derived

Its current precedence (`rheo-feed-updated`, then `output.date`, then output-file mtime — `feed.rs:117-133`) must stay as-is. It is tempting to "correct" it to prefer mtime now that `published` carries the authored date, but mtime changes on every rebuild, so every entry's `updated` would change on every deploy: feed readers would re-surface the entire archive as freshly modified after each build, and the feed-level `<updated>` (`max_updated`, `feed.rs:135-138` and `feed.rs:171`) would churn with it. Keeping `output.date` as the `updated` fallback keeps the feed stable.

Net effect of this bead: entries gain a `<published>`; their `<updated>` is byte-identical to before. Note this design point in a code comment so it is not "fixed" later.

## Tests

`crates/html/src/feed.rs:186+` already has a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with an `entry()` helper (`feed.rs:196-204`) that constructs `AtomEntry` literals — it needs the new field. Add assertions that:

- with `published: Some(_)`, the XML contains a `<published>` element with the RFC 3339 timestamp, distinct from `<updated>`;
- with `published: None`, no `<published>` element is emitted;
- `<updated>` is unchanged from the pre-change output for the same inputs.

Add a fixture test covering the `rheo-feed-published` var override, including the error path for a malformed RFC 3339 value.

## Docs

`rheo-feed-published` is a new author-facing variable — document it next to `rheo-feed-updated`, `rheo-feed-title` and `rheo-feed-exclude` in `rheo-author/SKILL.md` and on rheo.ohrg.org.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Entries built from a page with `#set document(date:)` carry both `<published>` (the document date) and `<updated>`.
2. Entries with no date and no override carry `<updated>` only, no `<published>`.
3. `rheo-feed-published` overrides the document date; a malformed value is a build error naming the variable.
4. For an unchanged project, every entry's `<updated>` and the feed-level `<updated>` are identical to the pre-change output.
5. The generated `feed.xml` validates against the W3C Feed Validation Service.
